nodes.title: Keep issues, comments, and PRs easy to scan
nodes.description:
Teammates have said that agent-written issues, comments, and PR descriptions are too long and too jargon-heavy to scan. This issue changes the writing rules: every issue and PR keeps a short plain-language summary first, and the agent's working detail moves into a section that Linear and GitHub render collapsed. Comments use one or two sentences to say what changed or was decided, with longer details in `🏗️ Agent notes`. The wording rules align with the house technical-writing guidance drafted in [hashintel/internal-agents PR #20](<https://github.com/hashintel/internal-agents/pull/20>). The change is ready for review in [brunch-lite PR #23](<https://github.com/hashintel/brunch-lite/pull/23>).

+++ 🏗️ Agent notes

Design settled 2026-08-19 in a working session with Lu. A scratch issue (FE-1450, since deleted) proved that the collapsed-section syntax survives create, read, update, and second-read operations in issue bodies and comments, and renders closed.

Changes to `docs/agents/issue-writing.md` and `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`:

* Root titles start with an active verb and name the task compactly. Planning and research remain valid tasks: use verbs such as `plan`, `map`, `decide`, or `test`. A title names an implementation only after that implementation becomes the agreed task.
* The visible summary is owned by the human driving the work, even when an agent writes on that person's behalf. An agent fetches and reads the current raw body before every change, preserves human edits, and never pushes a stale local draft. `🏗️ Agent notes` remains agent-maintained.
* When an issue comes from user, stakeholder, or teammate feedback, quote and link the source when the issue's audience can read it.
* The contract and execution record use one canonical collapsed-section label: `+++🏗️ Agent notes` in Linear and `<details><summary>🏗️ Agent notes</summary>` on GitHub. Copy the fixed string from the writing rules because the emoji carries U+FE0F.
* A comment's visible content states a decision or a change in confidence, risk, or scope in one or two short sentences. Implementation detail goes in `🏗️ Agent notes` in the comment or issue body. Progress narration stays in the issue body. The resolution comment keeps its length exemption: a verdict paragraph first, then `🏗️ Agent notes`.
* The technical-writing rules apply first. Industry-standard terms are free everywhere. Terms from technical literature belong in `🏗️ Agent notes` only when no plainer exact phrase fits; a visible summary also requires a definition and a `CONTEXT.md` entry. Do not coin a term for an issue. An inherited local term stays in `🏗️ Agent notes`.
* The org `technical-writing` skill in PR #20 above governs word choice; `issue-writing.md` governs structure. Its word list applies to all prose immediately, regardless of the PR's merge state. Exact machine text is exempt.
* Project updates reach the widest audience. They contain only a summary and the native health field, omit empty sections, and are drafted from issue-comment changes since the previous update. A `brunch-agent` project is planned as their home.
* `issue-tracker.md` says to read raw descriptions through `linear api` GraphQL rather than `issue view`, which prepends a header that corrupts a fetch, edit, and push operation. Linear's normalization of collapsed-section spacing and bullet markers is expected. Issue references use full URLs so Linear renders them as links.

Verification: `test/docs-index.test.ts` plus the repo's standard checks. This change edits Markdown only. The branch stacks on `ln/fe-1433-petrinaut-integration-spec` because the main worktree is occupied by another agent.

+++

nodes.title: A structured brunch question suspends and resumes visibly in Petrinaut
nodes.description:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

The next working prototype pulls the proven seams together and remains as the base for later demo work. In Petrinaut's real panel, the actual brunch agent invokes its existing structured `brunch_ask` affordance; a host-supplied component renders the current free-text form; submitting it resumes the suspended Flue conversation through `transport-aisdk`; and the next agent turn appears in the same panel.

This slice must settle provenance at the wire boundary. A human response submitted by the registered ask component travels in an AI SDK tool-output-shaped message, but it is not a machine tool result. Only a response matching the currently pending brunch ask and its stable tool-call id may be projected into the harness's user-affordance reply path; stale, forged, duplicate, or unrelated tool outputs must not become user evidence. Petrinaut mutation outputs remain non-user machine entries. FE-1395 will extend the form catalog later without replacing this transport distinction.

The prototype is deliberately legible: normal chat renders reasoning and text, the custom ask component renders its structured question and awaiting/submitted state, and an opt-in inspector or diagnostic surface shows request/turn boundaries, part kinds, correlation ids, suspension, return, and resumption. This observability is committed and tested, while remaining structurally excluded from evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The actual agent invokes `brunch_ask`; Petrinaut renders it through the host component; one submitted answer resumes the same Flue conversation and produces the next visible agent turn
- [ ] The current free-text affordance envelope and markdown floor are consumed without inventing the choice/questionnaire schemas owned by FE-1395
- [ ] Only the currently pending ask's correlated human submission becomes a user-affordance reply and may be cited as evidence; stale, forged, duplicate, and non-ask tool outputs fail or remain non-user
- [ ] Awaiting → submitted → resumed state and stable ids are visibly inspectable alongside the normal panel output
- [ ] The runnable integration, component registration, server path, and automated proof remain committed; the prototype requires no fetch shim or disposable harness
- [ ] Contract tests cover the translated ask part and return POST; a real-panel test or runnable story proves the custom component lifecycle

## Blocked by

* FE-1436 (durable real-panel transport and server path)
* FE-1448 (generic host-supplied interactive tool components in Petrinaut)
* FE-1422 (portable ask protocol in core)
* FE-1434 (suspension and machine-result provenance verdict)

## Coordination

FE-1395 owns the later form catalog and reserved structured-tap encoding. This slice proves the transport-level distinction and current free-text form only; FE-1395 consumes it rather than designing a second component mechanism.

nodes.title: Petrinaut hosts render their own interactive chat tools
nodes.description:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

Petrinaut hosts can supply custom interactive chat-tool components through the public `aiAssistant` configuration. Today the panel has the right internal pattern — an interactive-tool definition with input parsing, a widget, awaiting/submitted state, and `addToolOutput` submission — but its registry is private and hard-coded to Petrinaut's own `applyAutoLayout` tool. Unknown dynamic tools are rejected before a host can render or handle them.

Add a generic, typed host extension in `@hashintel/petrinaut` and prove it with a synthetic host tool in tests and a visible story or equivalent runnable surface. Built-in Petrinaut tools must keep their behavior; unknown unregistered tools must still fail loudly. This is durable product code in `hashintel/hash`, not a brunch-specific patch or a throwaway spike. It establishes the renderer/handler mechanism only; FE-1395 continues to own the final choice, questionnaire, absence-strip, and plugin-form catalog.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A host can register a tool name, input parser/schema, interactive React component, and submitted-output contract through the public `aiAssistant` API
- [ ] A registered dynamic tool renders inline with stable `toolCallId`, awaiting/submitted state, and exactly one submitted output available to the AI SDK follow-up
- [ ] Existing Petrinaut interactive and mutation tools are unchanged, and an unregistered dynamic tool still fails loudly
- [ ] The public type/API and lifecycle are documented and proved by focused tests plus a visible story or equivalent runnable example
- [ ] `@hashintel/petrinaut` contains no brunch-specific names, schemas, or components
- [ ] The implementation is committed on an isolated `hashintel/hash` branch; no temporary monkey-patch or browser shim is part of the proof

## Blocked by

None. FE-1435 is evidence for the current panel behavior, not a remaining execution blocker.

## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

The elicitor server runs on HASH infrastructure — owned jointly with infra, who confirmed Postgres exists and deployment is unblocked once the code lives in `hashintel/hash`. This adds a Postgres-backed storage-port implementation inside the binding (ADR-0002 N5: one implementation per binding × deploy target; the file-path assumption never leaks above the binding), and the public front door: per-principal and per-IP rate limiting plus a CORS origin allowlist, since the localStorage UID is identification, not authentication.

FE-1423 carries the ratified pre-remote gates and blocks this ticket: its auth gate is discharged by FE-1439, restart durability by FE-1396 (existing relation), but runtime telemetry and persisted-state versioning/backup remain FE-1423's own and must hold before the URL leaves the machine.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The server runs on HASH infrastructure with Postgres-backed storage behind the unchanged storage port
- [ ] Rate limiting (per-principal and per-IP) and the origin allowlist are active at the front door
- [ ] Every FE-1423 gate is checked off before public exposure
- [ ] The deployment target's specifics (host, CI, backup expectations) are recorded where infra work is recorded

## Blocked by

* FE-1439 (private sessions — the owner key and principal resolution this exposes publicly)
* FE-1437 (monorepo import — deployment presumes the code lives in `hashintel/hash`)
* FE-1423 (pre-remote gates — telemetry and state-versioning remain open there)

nodes.title: Elicitation sessions are private per browser and survive a reload
nodes.description:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

A visitor's elicitation is theirs: it survives a page reload, and another browser cannot see or alter it. The demo site mints a random UID into localStorage and sends it on every transport request; the host-authored server layer resolves principal → session set; the harness stays principal-free (session-id keyed). The storage port gains an **opaque owner key**, stamped at session creation — cross-principal access fails as a store-level refusal, the port's existing enforcement idiom, red-proved per the FE-1419 discipline.

The principal is deliberately ui-shell-owned (spec §4) so HASH's Ory identity can replace the localStorage UID later without touching the harness. The UID is identification, not authentication — the demo threat model accepts this; the front-door mitigations (rate limiting, origin allowlist) are the deployment ticket's. This ticket implements the auth/per-conversation-authorization gate of FE-1423 for the elicitor server. The kernel spec §9.6 owner-key amendment lands here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reloading the page resumes the same session and transcript; a different browser profile cannot read or write it
- [ ] The owner key is opaque to the binding; cross-principal refusals are proved red-first at the store seam
- [ ] The harness remains principal-free — no principal type appears in `core`
- [ ] Spec §9.6 gains the owner-key amendment in the same change
- [ ] FE-1423's auth gate is checked off with a pointer here

## Blocked by

* FE-1436 (conversation slice — the server and wire path this scopes)

nodes.title: The elicitor builds and repairs the net through Petrinaut's client-executed tools
nodes.description:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

The demo's central beat: answering the elicitor's questions makes the net appear and change on the Petrinaut canvas. The elicitor drives the panel's existing client-executed tool surface — the panel runs known tools against the live editor and posts the outputs back — via a new **external-tool round-trip protocol** in `core`, sitting beside the ask protocol on the same suspension floor and shaped by the suspension spike's verdict (FE-1434) on batch-vs-pending-slot.

The elicitor's Petrinaut tools are generated from `petrinaut-core`'s exported tool schemas, so the tool surface tracks Petrinaut's own contract rather than a hand-copied one. Provenance is a hard invariant: returned tool outputs enter as machine entries, mechanically excluded from evidence-span anchoring (§9.4) — capture spans only ever cite the user. Retries and duplicate dispatches are idempotent per the affordance-protocol guarantees FE-1420 establishes.

**Coordination note (soft, deliberate):** FE-1395's questionnaire chaining stands on the same pending-slot batching ground. Either may land first, but not concurrently by different agents — whichever lands first writes the §7.3/§7.4 amendment; the other consumes it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Answering in the panel produces net mutations on the canvas through client-executed tools, and the elicitor sees TypeScript diagnostics after code-writing mutations
- [ ] The round-trip protocol lives in `core`, tested substrate-free at the ask-protocol seam (FE-1422's extraction is the prior art)
- [ ] Tool schemas are generated from `petrinaut-core`'s contract, not hand-copied
- [ ] Returned tool outputs are machine entries: citing one as evidence is mechanically refused, red-proved
- [ ] A duplicate dispatch of the same tool outputs does not double-apply
- [ ] The §7.3/§7.4 amendment has landed — here or already via FE-1395, per the coordination rule

## Blocked by

* FE-1434 (suspension spike — the batch-binding verdict shapes the protocol)
* FE-1436 (conversation slice — the wire path this rides on)
* FE-1422 (ask protocol in core — the protocol home this extends)
* Coordinate with (not blocked by): FE-1395

nodes.description:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## What to build

The first durable tracer bullet: a locally-run Petrinaut panel holds a real conversation with the actual elicitor — text and reasoning only, no editor mutations yet. This turns the adapter spike's throwaway harness into production-intent code: a `transport-aisdk` package (the server end of the UI shell's reply transport — harness-level parts translated to UI-message-stream chunks, using the `ai` package for stream encoding only; inference stays on Pi's adapter layer) plus a thin host-authored server module around the harness.

The working integration is not a disposable prototype. Its server route, launch path, transport implementation, and verification fixtures are committed and become the base for the structured-ask and editor-tool slices. The local integration mode should make the protocol legible while it runs: request/turn boundaries, emitted part kinds, stable message/tool-call ids, and terminal state are observable without editing fixtures or attaching a debugger. That visibility is diagnostic metadata or an inspector surface; it must not be fed back as user evidence.

The wire seam becomes the contract-test surface here: tests drive the server exactly as the panel's wrapped transport does, replaying the spike's golden fixtures, so panel compatibility is provable without a browser. The kernel spec §12.2 amendment (the new `transport-*` role prefix and the package itself) lands in the same change — spec stays true to code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A locally-run panel (local `hashintel/hash` checkout) converses with the actual elicitor end to end
- [ ] The runnable server/transport path is committed production-intent code; no browser fetch shim or disposable server loop remains necessary
- [ ] `transport-aisdk` consumes harness-level parts only; the boundary gates prove it imports neither the binding nor Flue
- [ ] Wire-seam contract tests replay the golden fixtures against the real server — no browser in CI
- [ ] The local integration visibly exposes request/turn boundaries, emitted part kinds, stable ids, and completion state without laundering diagnostics into user evidence
- [ ] Kernel spec §12.2 gains the `transport-*` prefix and the new package in the same change (`adapter-*`/`wrapper-*` stay avoided terms)

## Blocked by

* FE-1435 (adapter spike — feasibility and the golden fixtures)

nodes.title: Spike: does a harness-driven stream drive Petrinaut's real chat panel?
nodes.description:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## Question

Can a server translating harness-level parts into the AI SDK v6 UI-message-stream protocol drive Petrinaut's real chat panel? The panel wraps whatever transport the host supplies with its own decorators, so the whole integration rests on our stream being indistinguishable from the stock one — text and reasoning render, server-executed tool parts render through the panel's default summaries, client tool calls execute against the live editor, and the diagnostics decorator fires.

This is the second gating spike. It is a throwaway prototype of the `transport-aisdk` layer, run against a local `hashintel/hash` checkout with zero commits there. Its transcript is the durable output: frozen as the golden fixtures the wire-seam contract tests replay from then on (freeze/replay posture per kernel spec §14.4).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The real panel renders streamed text and reasoning from the prototype server
- [ ] A client tool call round-trips: the panel executes it and posts the outputs back
- [ ] Server-executed tool parts render via the panel's default tool summaries
- [ ] The diagnostics decorator fires on the wrapped transport
- [ ] The full transcript (POST bodies including batched tool outputs; SSE chunk streams) is frozen as golden fixtures
- [ ] A written verdict; zero commits to `hashintel/hash`

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately, in parallel with the suspension spike (a fake server loop suffices; no suspension machinery needed).

nodes.title: Spike: does Flue turn suspension carry batched client-tool round-trips?
nodes.description:
## Parent

FE-1433 (the integration spec; ADR-0004 is the decision record).

## Question

Can Flue end a turn with client-tool calls pending and resume on a later dispatch — per-session state intact, the batched outputs re-entering the loop as machine entries? This is the first of the spec's two gating spikes: the external-tool round-trip is designed to ride the same suspension floor as the ask protocol (one substrate capability, two core protocols), and that only holds if the substrate carries the shape.

The verdict feeds two consumers: the external-tool round-trip protocol ticket (this graph) and FE-1395's questionnaire chaining, which stands on the same pending-slot batching ground. Failure here is not failure of the harness: it selects the spec's doc-handle fallback for the demo and files as evidence toward a `binding-pi`.

Spec: integration spec (FE-1433) testing decisions; kernel spec §7.3/§7.4 (suspension, one live affordance), §9.4 (provenance discrimination), §10 (binding capabilities).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A written verdict records whether terminate-with-pending plus resume-on-dispatch holds, referencing the probe code or transcript
- [ ] The verdict states whether batched outputs (several tool results in one dispatch) bind cleanly, and adjudicates batch-as-pending-slot-variant vs. a parallel channel — or names exactly what remains undecided for the protocol ticket
- [ ] Returned tool outputs demonstrably enter as non-user entries (never anchorable as evidence)
- [ ] Observed round-trip counts are noted against the tool-call-per-element scaling concern (survey §6d: a 40-place net is ~100 mutations)
- [ ] On failure: the doc-handle fallback is selected in writing and the evidence filed toward a second binding

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately. The spike is throwaway; only the verdict persists.

nodes.description:
The 2026-08-18 integration meeting settled the September demo's staging: the elicitor is presented inside [demo.petrinaut.org](<http://demo.petrinaut.org>)'s existing chat panel, not in a separate demo application. The brunch elicitor therefore runs as a remote server that Petrinaut's chat UI talks to through its host-pluggable transport, with the elicitor's sessions, captures, and IRs persisted server-side and keyed to the visitor's browser. The library is renamed `@hashintel/brunch-agent` and will be imported (with git history) into the `hashintel/hash` monorepo as a sibling of `@hashintel/petrinaut` once the currently open PRs merge.

This issue carries the integration spec for that architecture. The decision itself is recorded in ADR-0004 (`docs/adr/0004-in-petrinaut-staging-and-the-monorepo-import.md`), which supersedes the demo-shell recommendation (`docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/recommendation-demo-vehicle.md`). The spec document is at `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/petrinaut-integration-spec.md` — seams, user stories, implementation and testing decisions, and the spike-gated questions.

The two original spikes have now reported. Flue carries batched suspension through a non-user signal (FE-1434), and the AI SDK v6 wire shape drives Petrinaut's real panel (FE-1435). A third seam surfaced before implementation: Petrinaut's internal interactive-tool registry is not host-extensible, and a human answer returned through an AI SDK tool-output-shaped message must not be confused with a machine tool result. FE-1448 adds the generic host component mechanism; FE-1449 is the durable, visibly inspectable prototype that proves the actual brunch ask suspends and resumes without laundering provenance.

Related: FE-1333 (the integration-definition ticket this spec answers; closes on the ADR), FE-1357 (parent map).

---

nodes.title: Plugin authoring becomes declarative: a domain is two schemas and two tables
nodes.description:
Today every new elicitation domain looks like an engineering project: the capture store says how evidence is kept, but nothing says what a domain author must write down to make the machinery elicit *their* domain, and nothing turns a pile of typed captures into the thing the user wants — a model of their plant, their feature, their system. Completion questions ("is this model good enough to answer my objective?") have no model to be asked of, and semantic judgments risk hiding inside read paths where nobody can audit them.

The FE-1405 shapes work settled an answer, now written up as a provisional spec: a plugin is **two schemas and two small tables** — declare your domain's node kinds and slots, declare the typed proposals that fill them (annotated with how to elicit each), and say what your completion anchors demand; fold rules mostly derive. The elicited model is derived from captures by a pure fold (ADR-0003), all interpretation happens at write time as contestable captures, and model gaps mechanically cue grounded follow-up candidates. Interviewing strategy decides whether to ask, propose a likely structure for correction, or leave a visible gap. The spec is desk-validated on the baseline transcripts and cross-plugin thumbnails (Gherkin, formal verification, CPS); its ratification condition is a full worked pass across three plugin targets, and its open questions are carried as first-class sections with owning tickets rather than folded into the design.

---

nodes.title: The demo shell is safe to expose beyond localhost
nodes.description:
The mounted Flue agent route is public today: anyone who can reach the server can open or continue conversations under any conversation id. That is fine on localhost and disqualifying the moment the URL leaves the machine. This ticket carries the gates that must hold before the demo shell is exposed beyond localhost. It blocks remote exposure, not the demo itself.

Origin: the Flue-vs-tilde analysis's recommended course (`docs/reference/amp-analysis-flue-vs-tilde.md`), carried through the architecture cheatsheet's reconciliation section (`docs/planning/_shared/flue-architecture-cheatsheet.md`) and the routing table's pre-remote row (`docs/agents/flue-routing.md`), and tracked as Ledger A10 in `docs/planning/legibility-sweep/remediation-plan-2026-08-17.md`. On 2026-08-17 Lu ratified these as **requirements**, not recommendations — a demo deployment conversation with infra is already underway, so the gates are schedule-relevant now.

## Gates

- [ ] **Authentication + per-conversation authorization** on the mounted route — a caller can reach only conversations they own. Per the routing guide, auth belongs in app middleware around the explicit mounts in `app.ts`, not inside agents.
- [ ] **Runtime telemetry** — wire the `observe()` → OTel path so a remote failure is visible. Design note (Lu, 2026-08-17): inspection is the floor, not the ceiling — the intent is to incorporate traces (reasoning, skills, tool use) into our own feedback loops and oracles as we develop. Build the floor so it doesn't preclude that: structured, attributable spans, not just a liveness signal.
- [ ] **Persisted-state versioning and backup expectations** — decide what happens to durable state across our own schema changes (the capture store already parses on read; Flue's format versioning refuses to start on mismatch — our stance on migration vs. refusal is undecided), and what backup means on the chosen deploy target.
- [ ] **Restart durability** — owned by FE-1396 (blocking relation); listed here so the gate checklist is complete in one place.

## Deploy-target note

ADR-0002 rule N5 applies: a new deploy target means a new storage-port implementation inside the binding package (the Cloudflare case is per-object SQLite behind the same `CaptureStore` port). The file-path assumption never leaks above the binding.

nodes.title: The affordance protocol survives retries, unknown forms, and abandoned asks
nodes.description:
The FE-1389 deep-read (notes/deep-read-fe-1389.md, from the FE-1401 remediation sweep) found three places where the new ask/affordance protocol fails unsafely rather than safely. Flue re-executes tools at-least-once, and a re-executed ask mints the identical affordance — but the pending-slot guard checks only that the slot is occupied, so a benign retry is refused as if the model had asked a second question. The dev UI validates the whole concrete free-text form and renders nothing on a parse failure, so the first affordance of any other form will blank instead of falling back to the markdown floor the spec requires (§7.2/§7.7 — the envelope needs its own schema with the payload opaque). And an ask whose reply never arrives occupies the slot forever: nothing records an `unanswered` outcome (§7.5) and no advisory reports the stuck state (§8.6), so every later ask is refused silently.

None of these blocks the walking skeleton — they are the hardening it deliberately deferred — but the retry refusal will start firing as soon as anything (like the settlement trigger) makes re-execution common, and the markdown floor breaks the moment a second affordance form lands.

---

## Execution record

Findings, from the deep-read (file refs as of 81e9ce0):

1. **Retry misreported as duplicate ask** — `packages/binding-flue/src/index.ts` pending-slot updater tests `current !== null`; should tolerate `current.id === affordance.id` (id is deterministic in `toolCallId`, so re-execution is detectable). One-line fix + a test that replays the same tool call.
2. **Markdown floor absent in the UI** — `apps/dev/src/ui/chat.tsx` `safeParse(FreeTextAffordance, part.data)` returns null on failure. Needs an envelope-only schema (id / form / markdown, payload opaque) rendered as the fallback; ticket 10 §5 proved the intended behavior.
3. **No escape from an occupied slot** — slot clears only on `kind: 'user'` delivery; spec §7.5's `unanswered` outcome and §8.6's unaccounted-ask advisory are the intended relief valves, neither exists.

Source: docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/notes/deep-read-fe-1389.md (builder's account, "genuinely bug-shaped" items 1–3).

nodes.title: Catalogue the frontier-elicitor failure modes the published instruments cannot see
nodes.description:
## Question

**What are the failure modes of a frontier-model elicitor — catalogued at the level where our instruments can detect them and our machinery can be held accountable for preventing them?** The Bano/Ferrari taxonomy scored both baseline conditions nearly clean because it was built from human-novice mistakes; the failures that actually occurred (the pleasantry loop, deliverable deferral, silent hardening, the phantom-second-session exit, coverage blindness invisible to self-report) live outside its categories. [FE-1361](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1361/baseline-control-what-does-one-shot-ai-elicitation-already-achieve) demonstrated that our real adversary has a different failure distribution than any published instrument measures. Every future scoring pass — FE-1404's condition 3, the eventual evaluation proxy, regression checks when the substrate model upgrades — needs a taxonomy built from *this* distribution.

Seed entries from the baseline, each with its observed instance, its detection signature, and the machinery layer accountable for it: the pleasantry loop (interview over, deliverable never coming; no-progress detection); deliverable deferral behind self-prescribed data pulls (C1 — note the cause was a virtue: refusal to invent); the phantom commitment (C2's second session — see the nuance below); silent hardening (vague utterance → precise constant filed as confirmed; write-time epistemic status); never-asked coverage blindness (self-report structurally cannot see it; computed coverage); complementary-miss luck (one run's coverage is materially chance; same); the dead-artifact delivery (specification instead of loadable model; validate + project); invented-instrument leakage (the SHADE scale, the truck schedule — fabrications *inside* confirmed rows).

One entry needs care rather than prohibition: **deferral is not itself a failure**. The architecture supports multi-session elicitation against a target-document (sessions go quiet rather than close), and real practice has legitimate deferrals everywhere. The failure mode is *deferral without deposit* — deferring work without materializing it as stored state (typed `missing` issues, recorded absences, a re-entry briefing to inherit). C2's second-session move would have been *correct behavior* on the real architecture; it failed in the baseline because nothing persisted, so deferral equalled loss. The catalogue must distinguish licensed deferral (deposit made, adjudication updated) from evasive deferral (deferral substituting for adjudication), or condition 3's scoring will punish the wrong thing.

Method: sweep both baseline transcripts plus the literature's failure inventories (LLMREI's premature-ending, ReqElicitGym's budget exhaustion, Bano's residually-applicable items) into a typed catalogue: name, mechanism (why a trained-cooperative model produces it), detection signature (what an instrument or classifier looks for), accountable layer (disposition / technique / machinery, per the [FE-1361](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1361/baseline-control-what-does-one-shot-ai-elicitation-already-achieve) three-layer read), and prevention claim (which harness mechanism or pack element claims to prevent it — so each entry doubles as a testable claim against the September build).

Out of scope: building detectors or evals (the catalogue specifies them; the evaluation-proxy work builds them); fixing any failure mode.

Done when: the catalogue lands under `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/` with the seed entries elaborated and the transcript sweep done; FE-1404's scoring section references it; and each entry's prevention claim names the mechanism that will be held to it.

nodes.title: Design reusable elicitation strategies
nodes.description:
An elicitation should adapt to what the user is trying to achieve and how much effort they can give, instead of running through a fixed list of questions. The harness already names reusable interview situations, but it has no shared guidance for beginning an interview, proposing likely answers for correction, or deciding which uncertainties still warrant questions.

This issue will design reusable, domain-independent interviewing guidance. It includes an opening strategy that establishes the objective, its context and scope, and the user's available time, intended use, and tolerance for suggested assumptions within the first turn or two. It also covers proposing a broad draft for correction when time is short, while keeping confirmed statements, declared defaults, and unresolved suggestions visibly distinct.

+++ 🏗️ Agent notes

The kernel spec names this harness-side library the generic strategy quiver (§11.5). Guidance ownership follows vocabulary ownership: these cards teach how to work situations the shared capture envelope can name, while plugin cards teach what to notice in a domain. Plugins compose the shared cards into their packs at authoring time.

## Scope settled 2026-08-19

* Kickoff is a form the agent fills implicitly, not four literal questions. It establishes: objective; why and with respect to what; inclusion and exclusion boundaries; and the interaction posture inferred from available time, intended use, required confidence, and tolerance for agent-proposed assumptions.
* Optimize for low user effort to reach an acceptably grounded model, not for turn count. A one-turn questionnaire can score well on turns while making the experience worse.
* Strategy varies with the inferred posture: explore openly when appetite is high; synthesize and invite correction when it is constrained; propose low-risk structure and question only high-impact uncertainty in mixed cases.
* Proposal-and-correction is a generic strategy and an appetite-compensation strategy. A generated guess remains a suggestion until the user confirms or corrects it. Only declared plugin defaults may enter as `defaulted`; the IR must not present a model guess as user-grounded evidence.
* The shared capability set is: ask, propose, contrast, expose assumptions and gaps, capture corrections, and stop with visible gaps. The quiver says how to combine those capabilities. Plugins supply domain imperatives, target shapes, motifs, defaults, and the uncertainties that matter. The agent chooses among applicable strategies.
* The existing card set remains in scope: conflict, competing alternatives, ambiguity, weak or missing evidence, absence clusters, and choice-point pressure. Card form remains Detects / Goal / contrastive Questions / Artifacts unless this design pass finds that kickoff or proposal-and-correction needs a different form.

## Design seams to resolve

* The plugin contract's `firesWhen` table mechanically produces next-question candidates from model gaps. This issue must preserve those cues as candidates without turning the interview into a schema walk; kickoff also occurs before those slot-state cues exist.
* Session stopping and model completion are distinct. A constrained session may stop with a useful, structurally broad model containing confirmed proposals, declared defaults, and visible gaps.
* “Appetite” is a continuously inferred interaction posture, not necessarily a stored field or fixed user-facing mode.

## Prior design basis

The spec named but did not design the quiver, with milestone one shipping generic guidance in plugin packs. Reference shapes are ln-grill, ln-disambiguate, the `elicitation_style` trichotomy, and the assurance plugin's stress-the-argument split. [FE-1397](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1397) routed recurring choice-point technique to the quiver. [FE-1403](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1403) authors and tags envelope-vocabulary cards inside the CPS pack so they can graduate here.

Inputs when work starts: spec §11.5; the FE-1397 routing verdict and worked examples; FE-1403's tagged generic cards; the assurance plugin's §13.2 generic/domain decomposition; and the 2026-08-19 kickoff/appetite design discussion recorded above. Related: [FE-1357](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1357), [FE-1402](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1402), [FE-1403](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1403), [FE-1431](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1431).

+++

nodes.title: Draft the CPS payload interiors: annotated shapes for the ten kinds, worked from baseline utterances
nodes.description:
## Question

**What are the CPS payloads' interiors — and do answer-shaped fields carry the elicitation the way the catalog alone cannot?** The IR work validated kind *catalogs* (FE-1364, FE-1397): named kinds, prose "Holds" descriptions, projection targets. No worked example across all four targets drafts a field-level payload schema or a single concrete capture instance — as of today the payload type system is names over unstructured prose. The spec already demands more (§11.2, Principle v2: annotated shapes for everything produced; shallow wire schemas with deep requiredness in validators); nothing has scheduled it before the work that needs it.

And the rehearsal tickets need it: computed coverage can only see kind-level holes without fields; a completion contract can only adjudicate "an activity capture exists", never "this activity lacks its duration distribution"; clarification hints and the quantile protocol attach to fields, not kinds. This ticket therefore blocks FE-1402 and FE-1403.

The design tension to hold, from the evidence-granularity property: fields must be **answer-shaped, not artifact-shaped** — slots mirror what an expert can say (actor, inputs, outcome, duration-as-quantiles, the rationale attribute, absence-typed everywhere), never what the net needs (that factoring is `project`'s work). A schema whose unfilled slots read as natural next questions is doing elicitation-strategic work; a schema that mirrors Petrinaut's element fields is the granularity violation in type form.

Method, in the FE-1397 mold plus one grade harder: draft annotated shapes for the ten CPS kinds (the seven September-required kinds at full depth; the other three may stay shallow), then ground them in worked *instances* — take real utterances from the C1/C2 baseline transcripts and write the captures they should yield as concrete payloads, including at least one absence-valued, one quantile-carrying, one `prescribed|practiced`-split, and one multi-capture-per-utterance case. An utterance the schema cannot hold without distortion is a finding against the schema, not the utterance.

Out of scope: envelope changes (interiors live inside the opaque payload half); the Gherkin/BPMN interiors (the CPS set is the September design; siblings follow in plugin-spec authoring if the exercise bends Layer A, that is a finding to hand back).

Done when: annotated shapes for all ten kinds with per-field elicitation affordances (quantile-elicited, absence-typed, evidence-anchored, regime-attributed); a worked-instance set from real transcript utterances; any Layer-A friction recorded; and the shapes handed to FE-1402 (contract computes over fields) and FE-1403 (cards aim at fields).

nodes.title: Assemble the CPS pack's interviewing guidance and desk-test it where the baseline was weak
nodes.description:
## Question

**Does the imported interviewing guidance assemble into pack content that fires where the bare model is weak — and only there?** FE-1360 stocked the armory: four probe catalogues imported verbatim as ready pack content (CDM, ACTA, the 35-type typology, premortem), the two-phase interview architecture, the quantile/IDEA protocol for quantities. FE-1364 settled where guidance lives (ElicitationPack question-guidance; motif quiver scaffold-yes/generator-no). But nothing between here and plugin-spec authoring assembles that material into actual kernel cards (Detects / Goal / contrastive Questions / Artifacts) and clarification hints for the CPS plugin — the map currently has motif-quiver content scoped into "Plugin spec authoring", which means the first time the cards exist is inside the spec, unvalidated.

Cards aim at payload fields, not bare kinds: a card's Questions and Artifacts target the slots FE-1405 defines (an activity's missing duration quantiles, an unattributed regime, an absence left untyped), which is why this ticket is blocked by FE-1405 — without interiors the verdicts below go vacuous.

The baseline headline makes assembly a real design problem rather than transcription: the bare model already interviews objectives-first, probes unwritten rules, and keeps an assumptions register unprompted. A card that restates instinct is dead weight the elicitor pays for on every turn. So each drafted card needs a verdict against the transcripts: does it fire at a moment where the baseline demonstrably failed (the ramp-scrap hole that self-report couldn't see; the silent hardening of the truck schedule; the quantile protocol C2 only partially held), or does it fire where the bare model already succeeded (conflict-point depth, penalty-weight co-construction) and therefore needs demotion or deletion?

Per spec §11.5's milestone-one posture, generic technique ships inside this pack rather than being excluded: cards that operate on envelope vocabulary (conflict, ambiguity, weak evidence, absence clusters, choice-point pressure) are authored here alongside the domain cards, **tagged as envelope-vocabulary generics** so they can graduate to the harness quiver (FE-1406) instead of being lost in the CPS pack. The generic/domain split per card is itself a deliverable — the assurance plugin's §13.2 decomposition is the worked example.

Out of scope: designing the quiver as a harness capability (FE-1406 owns that); completion adjudication, which has its own ticket (FE-1402).

nodes.title: Decide when an elicitation is complete or should stop
nodes.description:
## Question

**Can a drafted completion contract adjudicate a real engagement — including ending it?** The baseline readout's gap #1 is the sharpest observed failure in the whole experiment: neither condition could end the engagement, and the two failure modes (C1's deliverable-deferral loop; C2's open-ended multi-session fiction) are both the absence of adjudication, not of reporting — the v0 checklist improved completeness *reporting* while nothing *adjudicated* it. The IR design commits to the mechanism's shape (question-relative completion anchored on `objective` captures over a static floor, interview opens on objectives) but not its computation: what "every objective has its supporting kinds covered" means operationally, what the floor checks, and what behavior the contract licenses when it is satisfied or stalled.

This is the same situation Layer A was in before FE-1397 — a ratified shape with an unvalidated interior — and it gets the same treatment: draft the computation, then rehearse it retroactively at the desk. The transcripts and the scoring materials already exist. Replay the drafted contract over both baseline transcripts (with the answer key as the coverage oracle) and record, per exchange: what the contract's state would have been, at which point it would have adjudicated done / not-done / stalled, and whether it catches the two observed failure modes. A contract that cannot stop the eleven-turn pleasantry loop, or that declares the C2 engagement complete while the ramp-scrap hole is open, fails the rehearsal.

Design input from [https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1406:](<https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1406:>) model completion and session stopping are distinct. A user with limited time may stop with a useful partial model, provided confirmed statements, declared defaults, assumptions, and remaining gaps stay visible. The rehearsal must therefore distinguish “complete enough for the objective” from “best useful result within this session's appetite,” rather than treating every early stop as completion or failure.

Out of scope: harness implementation (the contract's evaluation is a `project`-style read-time computation; September builds it), and any change to the envelope — this is plugin-payload and pack territory.

Done when: the contract computation is drafted at plugin-spec grade; a rehearsal memo scores it against both transcripts exchange-by-exchange; amendments from the rehearsal are folded back; the stopping result above is represented without weakening completion; and the result is handed to plugin-spec authoring alongside the FE-1397 handoff list.

nodes.title: Resolve the follow-ups from the stack legibility session
nodes.description:
I'm running a read-through of the open stack (FE-1374 up to FE-1390), aimed at regaining legibility over the top four branches before they land. The read-through is already surfacing more than branch understanding: process insights, a doc drift, and a couple of tooling ideas worth carrying forward. This issue is the resolution sweep for that session — everything we uncover, solve, design, or decide gets captured here and driven to a resolution, so the session's yield doesn't evaporate when the context does.

The session is in progress; items accrue below as they surface. Anything that grows real work graduates to its own sub-issue.

---

## Findings ledger

**1. CONTEXT.md authority-voice drift (fix).** The *Artifact boundary* glossary entry still opens "The decided integration posture between elicitor and Petrinaut (FE-1362)". The demo-vehicle posture is a recommendation to PM, not a ratified decision — FE-1363's entries carry the corrected voice ("recommended to PM, not ratified"), but the correction never propagated backward to the FE-1362-era entry beside them. Reword to recommendation voice; while there, scan the rest of the glossary for the same drift.

**2. Institute the cognitive-common-ground protocol (practice).** At the close of any work arc with significant agent-generated output, produce legibility artifacts that aid review and re-establish shared understanding — from plain-language/STE prose re-renderings up to exploded-view logic prototypes. FE-1374's spec renderings were the incidental prototype: re-rendering in a different register acted as a review instrument, and the round-2 read-through of those renderings fed four real changes back into the spec. Two parts: repeat the move within this session (a prose rendering of what the top four branches establish — FE-1390's capture-store semantics especially), and write the practice down (likely a `docs/agents/` home; exact placement open).

**3. Port ln-induct into dogsled as** `ds-induct` **(tooling).** The induction skill at `brunch/.agents/skills/ln-induct/` — treat point review-findings as samples from a latent fault-type, abstract to the lowest rung that is both mechanically searchable and names a repair, triage-gate before auditing — should be ported into the dogsled skill system, with graduation targets renamed to the dogsled family: `ds-code-review`'s Standards axis gains a contract/verification-integrity baseline section alongside the Fowler smells, each entry carrying *what it is → how to fix → how to probe* (these lenses are invisible in the hunk; they're detected by interrogation, e.g. "feed the gate nothing, demand red"). Graduation is two-tier and composing: prose priors accrue in dogsled and travel via plugin; per-repo, instances get pinned as categorical boundary tests wherever a mechanical predicate exists (the Dan Luu regression-capture principle). Repo-side wiring stays in CLAUDE.local.md only — the tracked repo must not depend on dogsled being present.

**4. Write up the two induced lenses with their evidence trails (graduation candidates).**

* *The vacuously green check* — a gate that passes because it inspected nothing. Three-PR recurrence: FE-1388 (`sourceFiles()` returning `[]` for unfamiliar layouts; decorative oxlint), FE-1399 (`workspacePackages()` passing every boundary invariant on an empty list), FE-1400 (vacuous build-artifact witnesses; CI gates matched against raw YAML text).
* *The parallel copy of a pinned truth* — the same fact maintained in two places, one drifting silently. Recurrence: FE-1399 (mount path now derives from `agentName`), FE-1400 (pinned-literal check routed through `pinnedIdentities`; expert's view derived instead of a parallel array; topology pin derived instead of hard-coded).

Each instance was caught by a fresh post-hoc review pass rather than by a standing lens at authoring time — that gap is the value the port in item 3 is meant to recover.

nodes.title: Close the review-found gaps where the gates, dev app, and baseline runner still fail silently
nodes.description:
During the FE-1397 tie-off, a full adversarially-verified review of the branch stack's diff against main surfaced ten confirmed correctness findings plus a handful of cleanups — none in the FE-1397 docs themselves, all in earlier branches' work. The common thread is uncomfortable: several of the checks FE-1399 added *to make silent failures loud* can themselves pass vacuously (a build-artifact witness matched by bootstrap code regardless of what got bundled, nested `test/` directories escaping every boundary invariant, a CI-gate check satisfied by commented-out gates, known-gap predicates that an empty stub file flips). Alongside those: the dev app's durable conversation store resolves its default path against the launch directory — the exact restart-durability failure the file's own comment says it exists to prevent — and the baseline runner can silently drop or truncate its main deliverable and dies on a single network blip hours into a paid run. The always-loaded agent instructions also still describe the triage roles as five verbatim labels, contradicting the rewritten triage doc's state/label mapping.

This ticket bundles all fixes as one refactor, executed as small always-green commits: documentation truth first, then the test-integrity fixes (each proven by temporarily breaking the guarded property and watching the gate go red), then the one behavioral dev-app fix, then baseline-runner robustness, then the cleanup tail. Filed from the FE-1397 thread's review output; to be claimed and run in a follow-up session.

---

## Commits (ordered by safety; each leaves the codebase green)

 1. Align the always-loaded agent instructions' triage one-liner with the triage doc's actual state/label mapping (only three roles remain labels; `needs-triage` and `wontfix` are workflow states).
 2. Replace the vacuous build-artifact witnesses with strings that only survive if the agent mount and the conversation-store module actually reached the bundle.
 3. Make the boundaries suite's first-statement check accept every directive form the workspace lexicon already declares legal, by reusing the shared directive pattern instead of a literal comparison; fold in the dedup of the pinned-identity and model-key regexes duplicated across the two suites.
 4. Make the workspace walker's source/test partition total: a file in a nested test directory is either governed by the test-hermeticity rules or included as source — nothing falls through silently. Red-proof with a fixture that previously escaped.
 5. Strengthen the CI-gate check to match against comment-stripped (or parsed) workflow steps so a disabled gate reads as absent.
 6. Re-encode the known-gaps predicates as "the verification actually runs" (content/execution checks) instead of "a file with this exact name exists", in both directions (stub files must not close a gap; differently-named real closures must).
 7. Anchor the dev app's default SQLite path to the module location instead of the working directory, mirroring how the UI root is already anchored; add a test asserting launch-directory independence.
 8. Baseline runner: widen code-fence matching (case, trailing space, digits/hyphens, CRLF) and warn loudly when no model artifact could be extracted despite a "delivered" verdict.
 9. Baseline runner: propagate the truncation flag through continuation stitching so an incomplete final delivery is marked incomplete and the operator is told the escape hatch exists.
10. Baseline runner: retry network-level failures and honor retry-after — preferably by replacing the hand-rolled HTTP client with the official Anthropic SDK, which also fixes the undercounted cache-token usage.
11. Cleanup tail, split as convenient: serve dev static assets via the framework's nested-path-capable routing and importable MIME table; un-hard-code the root build script's single-app filter; stop building the app twice per CI run and cache dependencies; remove the baseline runner's parallel message array and dead field; derive the boundary suite's package list instead of hard-coding it.

## Findings inventory (verified evidence; paths current as of the FE-1397 stack tip)

| # | Where | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `test/build-artifact.test.ts:82` | `toContain('createAgentRouter')` matches a preserved bootstrap JSDoc comment and `toContain('sqlite')` matches the bootstrap's unconditional default-adapter import — the test passes even if `app.ts`'s mount or `src/db.ts` never reach the build. Robust witnesses exist: the `app.route(...)` mount string and the `BRUNCH_DEV_DB_PATH`/`.data-wipe-me` strings unique to `db.ts`. |
| 2 | `test/workspace.ts:149` (with `:128`) | `sourceFiles()` prunes `test`/`tests`/`__tests__` at any depth while `testFiles()` only collects top-level test dirs — production code under e.g. `src/test/` escapes the substrate-import ban, schema-library check, and identity-duplication scan, and isn't governed by test-hermeticity either. |
| 3 | `apps/dev/src/db.ts:17` | Default store path `./.data-wipe-me/conversations.db` is cwd-relative; launching from a different directory silently creates a fresh empty DB. Anchor via `import.meta.url` as `app.ts` does for `uiRoot`. |
| 4 | `test/boundaries.test.ts:239` | First-statement check requires the literal `'use agent';` exactly, while `workspace.ts`'s `AGENT_DIRECTIVE_STATEMENT` (line 168) accepts both quote styles, optional semicolon, and trailing comments — forms the suite's own fixtures assert are legal fail spuriously. |
| 5 | `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/baseline/run.ts:213` | `largestCodeBlock`'s fence regex ```` /```[a-z]*\n/ ```` misses ```` ```JSON ````, trailing-space, digit/hyphen info strings, and CRLF — `writeArtifacts` (line 294) then skips the model artifact with no warning while the transcript header says delivered. |
| 6 | `run.ts:165` | Continuation stitching caps at 4 pieces and discards `result.truncated` — a still-truncated final delivery is written as complete; nothing tells the operator `--continue-final` was needed. |
| 7 | `run.ts:111` | Only HTTP 429/5xx are retried; a rejected `fetch` (TCP reset, DNS blip) crashes the run. Fixed `attempt*15s` backoff ignores `retry-after`. The hand-typed `ApiResponse` omits cache-token usage fields, undercounting cost. The official SDK replaces all of it. |
| 8 | `test/boundaries.test.ts:323` | CI-gate check is `workflow.includes(gate)` over raw YAML text — a commented-out or `if: false` gate still passes. |
| 9 | `test/known-gaps.ts:54` | Every `closed()` predicate is `existsSync` on one speculative future path: a real closure under another name stays "open" forever (banner rot), while `touch`ing the expected path closes the gap with nothing verified. |
| 10 | `AGENTS.md:19` (mirrored via `CLAUDE.md` symlink) | Says the five triage roles are "used verbatim as their own label strings"; `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` now maps `needs-triage` → state **Triage** and `wontfix` → state **Canceled**, leaving only three as labels. |

Cleanup tail (verified, lower stakes): `apps/dev/src/assets.ts` hand-rolled `:file` route can't match nested paths and duplicates hono's importable `getMimeType`; root `package.json` build script hard-codes `--filter '@brunch/dev'`; the full app build runs twice per CI run (build-artifact `beforeAll` + dedicated Build step) with no bun dependency cache; `run.ts` carries an `expertMessages` parallel array and a dead `interviewerTurns` field; `boundaries.test.ts` hard-codes the four-package list and two-scope substrate denylist.

## Decision document

* Modules touched: the repo-level verification suites (`test/`), the dev app's store and asset serving, the baseline runner script, the always-loaded agent instructions.
* No interface or schema changes; no production API surface exists yet. The one behavioral change visible outside tests is the dev store's default path resolution (env var override unchanged).
* Architectural stance: gate fixes must encode the *property*, not a proxy (witness strings unique to the guarded module; parsed rather than substring-matched workflow; executed-verification rather than file-existence). This is the FE-1399 charter applied to FE-1399's own checks.
* Baseline runner: prefer deleting the hand-rolled client in favor of the official SDK over patching it — fewer lines, retry/retry-after/typed usage for free. If the SDK dependency is unwanted in a planning script, the fallback is try/catch around fetch + retry-after parsing.

## Testing decisions

* Most of this work *is* the test layer, so the discipline is red-proofs: for each strengthened gate, temporarily introduce the violation it exists to catch (nested `src/test/` file importing the substrate; commented-out CI gate; stub gap file; missing db.ts in the bundle) and watch it fail before restoring green.
* The dev store path fix gets a unit test asserting the resolved path is launch-directory-independent; prior art in `apps/dev/test/assets.test.ts`.
* The baseline runner sits behind the typecheck gate only (FE-1361); extract its parsing helpers (`largestCodeBlock`, stitching) into testable pure functions if a red-proof is wanted, otherwise verify by targeted invocation — a full paid run is not required to exercise fence parsing.

## Out of scope

* The FE-1397 worked-examples docs and `ir-design.md` (no findings there).
* Redesigning the known-gaps mechanism itself — only the predicate strength changes.
* Anything inside `@flue/*` bootstrap behavior (the vacuous witnesses are our tests' problem, not Flue's).
* The refuted review candidates (resume double-count, sequential awaits, symlink-cycle walker, dev HMR gap, stale map pointer) — checked and dismissed, listed here so they aren't re-litigated.

nodes.title: Make the CI gates and dev app fail loudly where review found they fail silently
nodes.description:
The FE-1361 code review swept the whole repo and verified five findings that fall outside that ticket's scope. Three sit in the merge gates themselves: the checks that are supposed to keep workspace boundaries honest can currently go red on an innocent comment-only edit, silently skip any newly added workspace group, and let a misspelled tool operation name compile — so the gates either cry wolf or pass vacuously, which matters most in a repo whose gates are its main safety net. The other two are silent-failure seams in the dev app: a route path duplicates the one identifier the codebase pins as never-drifting, and the production asset route serves a narrower set of files than the client build can emit, so the first added font or image would break production only. All five have verified failure scenarios; each fix is small and none blocks current work.

---

## Findings (verified by the FE-1361 review, 2026-08-13)

1. `test/boundaries.test.ts:218` — agent-module detection is a bare substring match for `'use agent'` over raw file text, so a comment mentioning the directive turns any dev source file into an "agent module" and fails two assertions (CI red on a comment-only change; `test/build-artifact.test.ts:44` shares the filter). Fix: anchor detection to the first statement — the comment-stripping logic at lines 231–233 already exists.
2. `test/workspace.ts:49` — `workspacePackages()` hardcodes `[packages, apps]` instead of deriving from (or asserting agreement with) root `package.json`'s `workspaces` globs, so a new workspace group escapes every boundary invariant as a vacuous pass; `directoriesIn()` also returns `[]` for a missing parent, so a renamed group degrades silently. Fix: assert the hardcoded group set equals the workspaces globs.
3. `packages/core/src/naming.ts:60` — `toolName(operation)` takes plain `string` instead of the `Operation` union exported two lines above (the union has zero consumers), so `toolName('aks')` compiles and ships a misnamed model-facing tool. Fix: narrow the parameter type.
4. `apps/dev/src/app.ts:19` — the mount path hardcodes `'brunch-gherkin-elicitor'` although `GherkinElicitor.agentName` is imported in the same file; a copy-pasted second agent would shadow the mount while tests stay green. Fix: `` app.route(`/agents/${GherkinElicitor.agentName}`, …) ``.
5. `apps/dev/src/app.ts:36` — the production `/assets/:file` route allowlists only `.js|.css|.map` and reads hits as UTF-8, so any other emitted asset 404s in production (works in vite dev), and extending the allowlist without switching to a Buffer read would corrupt binary bytes.

Full verdicts and failure scenarios are in the FE-1361 review record; the two findings that touched FE-1361's own files (typecheck-gate coverage, migrated-doc links) were fixed on its branch and are not part of this ticket.

nodes.title: Re-entry briefing, resume reconciliation, and restart durability
nodes.description:
## What to build

Coming back. Quit an interview halfway, restart the process, return later, and the agent picks up knowing what changed while it was away — what was captured or superseded, which issues opened or closed, what was left unswept, and which question is still hanging. It says so in the conversation rather than pretending continuity.

The subtle requirement is that the briefing must be in the log honestly without ever becoming evidence. It is injected on the user's behalf, so it looks like the user's side of the conversation — and a capture citing it would launder the system's own words into the person's mouth.

Spec: §9.1–9.3 (durable document, per-session state, re-entry briefing), §9.4 (provenance), §9.5 (completion derived), §8.7 (resume-time sweep reconciliation), §14.5 (restart durability).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resuming a session after the world moved injects a state message whose content is computed facts only: unswept tail, captures created or superseded and issues opened or closed since this session last swept, open issues, pending unanswered affordance
- [ ] The briefing is advisory — it forces nothing, and the agent weighs it
- [ ] A minimal user-visible insertion notice accompanies every injected state message
- [ ] Injected entries project as structurally non-user, so citing one as evidence is mechanically refused rather than merely discouraged
- [ ] An unswept tail left by a session that ended between judgment and sweep surfaces on resume, and the agent judges whether to sweep before proceeding
- [ ] The briefing works in all three shapes: fresh session, resumed session, and post-restart
- [ ] Full-stack durability holds with a real conversation store: captures, session logs, high-water mark, and pending slot all survive a process restart
- [ ] A new session binds to its target-document through immutable creation data; dispatching an existing conversation id resumes against the document's current state
- [ ] Completion is a read-time derived status with no lock and no terminal state — someone returning with a correction after "done" is handled normally

nodes.title: The full affordance set — choices, questionnaire chaining, and the absence strip
nodes.description:
## What to build

The rest of the ways the harness can ask something. Beyond free text: pick one, pick several, and a questionnaire that walks several questions locally without a model turn between them. Plus the absence strip — the one-tap way to say "I don't know", "doesn't apply", or "decide later" — and the transport mechanism that makes a tap genuinely distinguishable from typed prose.

That last part is load-bearing and easy to get wrong. Inbound replies are string-only, so a bare string cannot tell a one-tap "not applicable" from someone typing the words. Tap-ness has to be a transport fact or the system will claim certainty it hasn't earned.

Spec: §7.2 (baseline forms, questionnaire chaining, markdown floor), §5.1 (absence states, reserved reply encoding), §7.7 (recorded transport facts).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single-choice and multi-choice questions work end to end, rendering and returning through the same evidence path as free text
- [ ] A questionnaire is one affordance with N steps: the payload carries all the questions, the ui walks them locally, answers return individually or batched, and no intermediate model turns occur
- [ ] The absence strip's three labels map onto their absence states, and absences land as first-class capture values
- [ ] A reply parsing as the reserved encoding, arriving while its affordance is pending, is transport-explicit; every other reply is conversational and yields absences marked inferred
- [ ] Structured taps are optional for a ui, not required: a ui affording only the markdown floor produces no encoding and honestly yields inferred-only absences
- [ ] Plugin custom forms register as progressive enhancement keyed on form tag, with payloads opaque at the tool boundary and validated harness-side against plugin declarations on read-back
- [ ] Every form carries a markdown floor
- [ ] Deferred and declined behave differently downstream: completion evaluation chases a deferral and treats a decline as a boundary that only an explicit act can close

nodes.title: Conflict, supersession, and the interpretation render
nodes.description:
## What to build

What happens when someone changes their mind or contradicts themselves. Say something, say something incompatible later, and both readings stay live and visible until you explicitly settle which one holds — the system never quietly picks. Alongside it, the one affordance the harness must own itself: the render that shows you what it thinks you said, with the uncertainty intact.

Spec: §6.3 (issues versus advisories), §7.5 (transport outcomes), §7.6 (interpretation render), §8.4–8.5 (supersession channels, resolution records).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contradicting yourself surfaces a `conflicting` issue with both interpretations live as alternatives, and neither is silently dropped
- [ ] Resolving it produces a resolution record citing your own words; the winning capture keeps its original epistemic status and authority lives in the record
- [ ] The two supersession channels are distinguishable in the store: a creation-time link for sweep-time correction, a resolution record for issue-time adjudication between existing alternatives
- [ ] The interpretation render is harness-owned and shows envelope vocabulary — epistemic status, absence states, live alternatives, derived status — with a plain JSON default and a plugin-optional typed renderer seam that is actually exercised by the gherkin plugin
- [ ] Non-interactive renders ride their own tool output parts and never contend for the affordance slot, so an ask and a render in one batch cannot clobber each other
- [ ] Transport outcomes record as answered, redirected, or unanswered, distinct from epistemic absence; a topic change mid-question reads as redirected
- [ ] Advisories are computed and ephemeral — never stored, never blocking — and issues are stored and close only explicitly
- [ ] Harness invariants 1, 2, and 6 hold as executable tests

nodes.title: Plugin SDK and the gherkin plugin — the first projected artifact
nodes.description:
## What to build

The first end-to-end artifact. Someone is interviewed about a feature and gets back a valid Gherkin feature file, together with an honest report of everything they said that the file could not represent. This is where the plugin contract stops being a design and starts being something a plugin author actually programs against.

**Explicit non-goal: this ticket does not freeze the plugin contract.** Gherkin is the trivial target, and the spec's two-targets rule forbids letting it fix the interface before a hard target has stressed it. Build the SDK surface, exercise it, and leave it declared unstable.

Spec: §6.1 (operations and calling convention), §4 (inversion of control, PluginContext), §11.1–11.3 (what a plugin owns, pack form, smallest honest plugin), §13.1 (gherkin).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An interview about a feature yields a parse-valid `.feature` file plus a typed loss report using the declared vocabulary
- [ ] The four operations are pure and snapshot-in/deltas-out: they receive an immutable snapshot and return observations, issues, and deltas; the harness validates and applies; no operation addresses storage, the user, or the model
- [ ] Harness capabilities reach the plugin only through a narrow injected PluginContext, and milestone one defines no storage-addressable methods on it at all
- [ ] The plugin ships an ElicitationPack — kernel cards, completion contract, clarification hints — and a ProjectionPack with required project and validate, authored to the `writing-for-agents` standard and Principle v2
- [ ] Validation is parse validity plus an optional pack-declared step-lexicon check, needing no external project
- [ ] Validators are total: they never throw, and always return typed issues
- [ ] Issues are namespaced to their producer, so a target-originated requirement never silently reads as a harness-level one
- [ ] A failed operation leaves no partially applied deltas
- [ ] The smallest-honest-plugin bar is checked, not assumed: a flat record list plus one validator must suffice, and every contract addition made here is justified against the bar it raises
- [ ] The SDK export surface is documented as unstable pending a second target

nodes.title: Settlement trigger and sweep — the first captured statement
nodes.description:
## What to build

The slice the whole architecture is for. You say something in conversation; the agent judges that the topic has closed; it sweeps what you said into the store as captures anchored to your actual words; and the sweep is safe to run twice. After this ticket the system genuinely elicits — it just has nothing domain-shaped to do with the result yet.

Spec: §8.1 (settlement trigger and judgment), §8.3 (sweep idempotence), §8.6 (unaccounted-ask advisory), §6.4 (cadence as policy), §10 capabilities 7 and 9.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A conversation about something substantive produces captures in the store, each anchored to a verbatim quote from the person's own turns
- [ ] Settlement decomposes into trigger and judgment: the harness computes the unswept tail and steers a settlement-check signal into a same-response continuation turn; the agent decides whether the range has settled, and declining is legal
- [ ] The trigger's two guards hold — it fires on suspensions too, so a pending affordance suppresses the nudge; and it never re-nudges the same latest user entry
- [ ] Re-sweeping a range creates no duplicate captures and does repair omissions, because identity is content-keyed rather than range-keyed — load-bearing under at-least-once tool re-execution
- [ ] A sweep containing an ask with no reply and no capture citing it reports the fact as an advisory and blocks nothing
- [ ] The swept high-water mark advances as per-session state and survives independently of the transcript
- [ ] Running projection and validation at read time rather than at sweep completion changes no outcome

nodes.title: Durable entry projection, harness-resolved anchoring, and the session-log archive
nodes.description:
## What to build

The bridge between a live conversation and the store: given a session someone has actually talked into, the harness can take a verbatim quote and work out which entry it came from — and can keep those entries retrievable forever, independently of whatever the substrate decides to retain.

This exists because the model cannot be trusted with entry numbers and can be trusted with quotes. Ticket 13's HITL rounds on the prior map found the model's quotes flawless and its sequence guesses never once convergent, so anchoring is harness-resolved and entry identity never appears in the model-facing contract.

Spec: §5 (evidence spans), §8.2 (harness-resolved anchoring), §9.4 (provenance), §9.6 (session-log archive), §10 capability 8.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The binding can read the session's durable entry projection with provenance-discriminating entry kinds, absorbing the absence of an in-process API
- [ ] A verbatim quote resolves to an entry pointer against true-user entries only; the stored span carries both excerpt and pointer, resolved exactly once at application time
- [ ] No match refuses with a repair hint rather than guessing; multiple matches anchor the latest and attach an advisory note
- [ ] Sequence numbers and range bounds appear nowhere in the model-facing tool contract
- [ ] A capture citing an injected non-user entry is refused at validation
- [ ] Archive-on-read holds: every entry the binding reads is retained in the target-document store, and every entry a capture points to is retrievable from the archive indefinitely
- [ ] Base-URL discovery for the history projection is resolved rather than hardcoded, and paging behaviour beyond a thousand entries is either handled or explicitly bounded with a recorded finding

nodes.title: Capture envelope, storage port, and the local capture store
nodes.description:
## What to build

The capture store and the envelope that sits in it — drivable end to end from tests with no model and no substrate, which is the whole point of the design. You can write a capture, correct it, contradict it, retract it, and read back a coherent history in which nothing was silently overwritten and every status was computed rather than stored.

Spec: §5 (capture envelope), §5.1 (absence states), §6.2 (envelope-level validation), §8.3–8.5 (idempotence, supersession, resolution records), §9.6 (the storage port), §10 capability 10.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The storage port is harness-defined and binding-implemented; nothing in the plugin surface can reach persistence
- [ ] The envelope carries a harness-minted id alongside a content-derived dedup key that excludes epistemic status, so re-reading the same evidence differently requires explicit supersession
- [ ] Value-XOR-absence is enforced as a refusal, and the six absence states are distinct capture values that never collapse into null or negation
- [ ] Supersession is single-hop over active heads only; superseding an already-superseded capture is refused, and that refusal carries the world-moved facts
- [ ] Superseded captures stay inspectable forever and never read as active
- [ ] A `conflicting` issue closes only through a resolution record citing the true user's utterance; a bare close is refused, and so is a record citing the agent's words
- [ ] Retraction is an explicit stored event citing the user, naming no successor, and is the only path to retracted status
- [ ] No status field is stored anywhere — envelope status derives at read time from links, records, and events
- [ ] Writes are serialized and application is whole-sweep-atomic: a sweep applies entirely or refuses entirely
- [ ] Harness invariants 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, and 10 hold as executable tests

nodes.title: Walking skeleton — the harness asks a free-text question and binds the reply
nodes.description:
## What to build

The first thing a person can actually use: open the dev app, and the agent asks a free-text question, waits, receives the typed answer, and carries on the conversation with the answer in hand. This is the turn-suspension protocol the harness has to own because Flue has no ask-the-user primitive, proven in the real tree rather than on a prototype branch.

The prototype on `prototype/10-flue-roundtrip` already established the mechanism; this ports it in and hardens the two rulings that came after it — no instruction interpolation, and mechanical reply binding.

Spec: §7.1–7.4, §7.7, §9.2 (pending-affordance slot), §10 capabilities 1–5, §12.1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A person can hold a multi-turn conversation in the dev app in which the agent asks free-text questions and receives answers
- [ ] Turn suspension works through a terminating ask tool plus the pending affordance in per-session state, with the answer arriving as a fresh dispatch
- [ ] The pending question is never interpolated into instructions — it rides the ask tool's result — and no "instructions updated" advisory wake occurs per ask (spec §14.5 wake-wart residue: confirm no other instruction-state write path re-triggers it)
- [ ] Reply binding is harness-mechanical off the single-pending invariant: no echo token, no reliance on the model remembering an id
- [ ] Durable affordance identity and payload ride the ask tool's output part, not the data channel
- [ ] A second interactive affordance in the same batch is rejected as mechanism, not as instruction
- [ ] Every question renders through the markdown floor, so a ui that knows only the envelope shows something usable

## What to build

A Bun-workspace monorepo that builds and tests green from empty, with the architectural boundaries in place from the first commit rather than retrofitted later. Nothing user-visible happens yet; what this delivers is that every later slice lands into a structure that already refuses the wrong dependency direction.

- [ ] `bun test` and `vite build` both pass from a clean checkout, with no model key and no network access
- [ ] Packages exist per the spec's topology with its role prefixes: `core` (plugin SDK as its export surface) with a `core/testing` subpath, `binding-flue`, `plugin-gherkin`, and a dev app owning the agent module, mount, and conversation store
- [ ] The dependency invariants hold and are mechanically checkable, not just documented: plugins resolve `core` only — never the binding, never Flue; `core` imports no substrate; the binding imports both
- [ ] Valibot is the schema library at every boundary; no Standard-Schema conversion seam
- [ ] The recorded Flue constraints are respected by construction: vite pinned to ^8, `'use agent'` as the agent module's first statement, `agentName` a pinned string literal
